lines: Public notices can change. Documents can disappear.
And after the fact, it can be difficult to establish which version was actually observed.
Sakshi creates a verifiable record of document observations, using Arkiv.
Sakshi is an independent witness archive for public recruitment and examination notices.
It records document observations on-chain, and lets anyone compare a file against the evidence that was recorded.
This demonstration uses synthetic notices, so we can reproduce changes and removals consistently.
The evidence records themselves are real Arkiv Tiramisu records.
Sakshi hashes the supplied document on your device, and checks for a matching observation.
A matching hash identifies recorded evidence for that file.
A changed hash shows that the files differ, and a removed notice is reported as removed.
And if no qualifying record is found, Sakshi reports that limitation, rather than inventing certainty.
Sakshi supports multiple witness identities.
For this notice, both addresses have matching observations.
Excluding witness B leaves one trusted witness. Excluding both leaves no qualifying observation.
Both addresses are operated by the same team, so they are distinct identities, not independent organisations.
The timeline makes document changes observable.
It records what was observed, and when, without pretending that a hash alone establishes intent or authenticity.
The same verification is available from the command line, so the evidence can be inspected outside the browser.
These observations are recorded on Arkiv Tiramisu.
The transaction and creator can be inspected independently of the Sakshi interface.
Sakshi makes document observations verifiable, and changes traceable.
It gives people evidence they can inspect.
